Going to (4,1,6) leaves no safe move afterwards; going to (4,4,7), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes to (2,2,7).
Going to number 2, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,2,4). So the line goes to (1,2,6).
Number 2 is only reachable this way.

Going to (4,4,1) would leave number 9 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (1,4,2) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (2,6,1).
Number 9 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (1,4,6), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,6,6). So the line goes to (1,6,4).
The line must go to (1,6,6): to (2,7,4) is number 18, which comes later.
Cell (1,4,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,4,7).
Going to (2,6,7), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (4,4,7).
Going to (6,4,7), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (4,6,7).
Cell (2,6,7) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,7,6).
Going to (4,7,4) would force the line onto number 18 before its turn. So the line goes to (6,7,6).
The line must go to (7,6,6): to (6,7,4) is number 17, which comes later; to (6,6,7) is number 25, which comes later.
Going to (7,6,2), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (7,4,4).
Going to (7,2,4) would leave number 16 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,4,2).
Going to (7,6,2), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,6,1). So the line goes to (6,4,1).
Going to (4,4,1) would cut off a group of 9 cells; going to (6,2,1) would leave number 17 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (6,6,1).
Cell (7,6,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,7,2).
Going to (4,7,2) would leave both number 19 and number 20 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (6,7,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,7,4).
Going to (4,7,2) would leave both number 19 and number 20 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (2,7,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,7,2).
Cell (4,1,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,1,2).
Cell (6,2,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,2,2).
Going to (7,2,6) would force the line onto number 24 before its turn. So the line goes to (6,1,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,1,6).
Going to (7,2,6) would leave both number 24 and cell (6,2,7) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (6,2,7).
Cell (7,2,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,4,6).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
